source.title: The Andre-Oort conjecture for A_g
readSections: All 12 PDF pages inspected using rendered screenshots

summary: Source-grounded checkpoint covering the published proof of Andre-Oort for A_g: primitive maximal-CM orbit bounds from averaged Colmez and quantitative isogenies, the field-of-moduli/definition bridge, the reduction to arbitrary CM orders, and the Pila-Zannier counting argument. LD.6 already owns the Andre-Oort application: a duplicate standalone Andre-Oort roadmap is not justified. Stable-height and CM-type/reflex-norm foundations have existing owners. The reviewed aggregate audit was inaccessible and several external proof interfaces remain unchecked, so missing statuses and new Part-II ownership are provisional and this is not a complete extraction.

provenance.sourcePdfSha256Note: Published PDF was read through browser text and screenshots; binary download attempts failed. No checksum is invented.
provenance.supersededWorkingNote: An initial draft cited different CM-field declaration names and a Galois-only regulator theorem. A fresh read at the actual pin corrected both. Only the current references in items are authoritative.

items.name: CM fields and their maximal real subfields
items.statement: A number field E is CM when it is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field E0. Write [E:Q]=2g and [E0:Q]=g. E need not be Galois over Q.
items.note: Pinned source rechecked directly: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, blob 6c7067617742aae433a648031822e84a41746b4f, lines 63-91. The class assumes Field and CharZero and requires a totally complex quadratic extension of the maximal real subfield. No Lean elaboration was run.

items.name: CM types
items.statement: For a CM field E, a CM type Phi selects one embedding E -> C from each conjugate pair; it has cardinality g. The type of an O_E-action on an abelian variety is its action on the tangent space at the origin.
items.note: Import the CM.0 type API; do not replace a type by an unordered collection with multiplicities.

items.name: Primitive CM types
items.statement: A CM type is primitive if it is not induced, by restriction of embeddings, from a CM type on a proper CM subfield of E.

items.name: The CM class set S(E,Phi)
items.statement: S(E,Phi) is the set of O_E-equivariant isomorphism classes of dimension-g abelian varieties over C with an injective O_E-action of tangent type Phi. Its objects and isomorphisms are not principally polarized objects unless that extra datum is explicitly imposed.
items.note: Keep the class set used for ideal-isogeny counting distinct from the polarized point used for the field of moduli.

items.name: Field of moduli of a polarized abelian variety
items.statement: For a polarized abelian variety over Qbar, define its field of moduli through the stabilizer of its polarized isomorphism class in Gal(Qbar/Q), equivalently the residue field of the associated coarse moduli point. This is not automatically a field of definition.
items.note: The descent bridge is a separate theorem below; do not equip this field with a model by definition.

items.name: The Hodge determinant and its archimedean norm
items.statement: For an abelian variety A/K with everywhere semistable reduction, take the determinant of invariant differentials of its Neron model over O_K. At each complex embedding use the integral of omega wedge conjugate(omega) to define the metric entering the paper's Faltings-height normalization.
items.note: Import semistable Neron models and determinant-line arithmetic from their existing owners.

items.name: Stable Faltings height
items.statement: With L the Hodge line and nonzero omega in H0(L), define h_F(A) as (log # (H0(L)/O_K omega) - (1/2) sum_sigma log |integral_{A_sigma(C)} sigma(omega wedge conjugate(omega))|)/[K:Q], after a field extension giving everywhere semistable reduction.

items.name: Independence of the Hodge section
items.statement: The height expression is unchanged on replacing the nonzero Hodge section omega by another nonzero section; the product formula compensates the finite-index and archimedean changes.

items.name: Stable height and change of field
items.statement: After semistable reduction, the normalized expression is invariant under further finite extensions, hence defines a stable height independent of the chosen semistable field. Existence of such an extension is an imported theorem, not an assumption that every initial model is semistable.

items.name: Dimension-uniform lower bound for Faltings height
items.statement: For each g there is a real constant c_g such that h_F(A) >= c_g for every g-dimensional abelian variety over Qbar; the paper also records linear dependence on g. The lower bound need not be positive.
items.note: Needed to isolate one CM height in the averaged formula. The word positive later in the proof must not become a false positivity theorem.

items.name: CM classes and the ideal class group
items.statement: For a CM field E and CM type Phi, the O_E-equivariant CM class set is nonempty and has cardinality h_E = #Cl(E), through the CM lattice/ideal-class classification.
items.note: This is the unpolarized equivariant class set, not the number of principally polarized CM moduli points.

items.name: Brauer-Siegel in bounded degree
items.statement: For number fields of bounded degree and absolute discriminant D tending to infinity, log(h_K R_K) = (1/2+o(1)) log D. Make the uniform fixed-degree interpretation and possibly ineffective constants explicit.
items.note: The inspected EffectiveBounds roadmap targets effective small-class-number bounds; its long-term Brauer-Siegel aspiration is not an established library theorem or a precise replacement for this input.

items.name: Discriminants of CM extensions
items.statement: For a CM field E with maximal real subfield E0, |Disc(E)| = |Disc(E0)|^2 N_{E0/Q}(d_{E/E0}), hence |Disc(E)| >= |Disc(E0)|^2.
items.note: Elementary number-field import; marked missing provisionally until the reviewed audit and exact pinned declaration are reconciled, not a claim that no such library theorem exists.

items.name: Uniform comparison of CM and real regulators
items.statement: For arbitrary CM E of degree 2g, the regulator of E differs from that of E0 by a factor bounded above and below solely in terms of g, via the Hasse unit index and the conventional power of 2. Equality of regulators is not required.
items.note: CORRECTION after a fresh pinned-file read: the general CM regulator comparison IS present, without an IsGalois Q E hypothesis. In blob 6c7067617742aae433a648031822e84a41746b4f, lines 365-380 prove indexRealUnits is 1 or 2, and lines 440-445 give regulator E / regulator E0 = 2^(Units.rank E) / indexRealUnits E under NumberField E and IsCMField E. The earlier working note about a Galois-only regulator_ratio declaration was wrong and must not be reused. The paper's informal equality is replaced by this exact existing formula, not by a new development.

items.name: Lower bound for the CM class-number quotient
items.statement: For fixed g and every epsilon>0, there are positive constants C and D0 such that h_E/h_E0 >= C |Disc(E)|^(1/4-epsilon) for CM fields of degree 2g and discriminant at least D0.

items.name: Endomorphisms for primitive maximal CM
items.statement: For primitive Phi and A in S(E,Phi), End_C(A)=O_E with the specified action, and isogenies between members of this fixed-type class set respect that action.
items.note: Keep the fixed type and maximal order hypotheses; this is not a statement about arbitrary CM abelian varieties.

items.name: The quotient isogeny attached to an ideal
items.statement: For nonzero integral I in O_E and A with O_E-action, form T_I as the common kernel of the endomorphisms in I and the quotient isogeny A -> A/T_I. Record equivariance, finite subgroup-scheme descent, and the target CM type.

items.name: Ideal norm equals isogeny degree
items.statement: Under the fixed primitive maximal-CM hypotheses, nonzero integral ideals parameterize the relevant target-and-isogeny pairs, the isogeny attached to I has degree N(I), and all members of S(E,Phi) are mutually isogenous.

items.name: Uniform counting of bounded-norm ideals
items.statement: For degree 2g fixed and every epsilon>0, the number of integral ideals of norm n is O_{g,epsilon}(n^epsilon); consequently the number of ideals of norm <=X is O_{g,epsilon}(X^(1+epsilon)). Constants must be uniform in E.
items.note: A divisor-function estimate supplies this input; do not use a constant depending on the particular field in the discriminant argument.

items.name: A pair requiring a large-degree isogeny
items.statement: For fixed g and epsilon>0, a primitive maximal-CM class set S(E,Phi) contains A,B for which every complex isogeny A -> B has degree >= C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^(1/4-epsilon), after the usual small-discriminant adjustment.
items.note: The printed proposition states existence of a pair. Its preceding proof fixes A arbitrarily, so retain the strengthened interface: for each A there is a distant B. That version proves the moduli-degree bound for every A, not just one representative.

items.name: Masser-Wustholz isogeny estimate with field degree
items.statement: For each g there are positive C_g,kappa_g such that geometrically isogenous g-dimensional abelian varieties A,B both defined over a number field k admit a complex isogeny of degree <= C_g max(1,h_F(A),[k:Q])^kappa_g. No preservation of the chosen polarization is imposed.
items.locator: Theorem 2.3, p. 383; [12], Theorem II and field-degree discussion
items.note: The max includes 1 to avoid a sign issue. Inspected [12], printed pp. 7 and 24: polarization dependence is removed by Zarhin's trick; the field-degree estimates supply uniform constants. R28.4's qualitative Tate isogeny theorem does not cover this estimate.

items.name: Faltings height depends only on the CM type
items.statement: For fixed E,Phi, all members of S(E,Phi) have the same stable Faltings height, denoted h_F(E,Phi).

items.name: Character data for Colmez heights
items.statement: For the normal closure of a CM field and a CM type, form the rational character coefficients c_{rho,Phi} and the Artin conductors f_rho occurring in Colmez's formula, with the same representation, conjugation, and L-function conventions as the cited source.
items.note: The individual Colmez conjecture is context, not a proved input. A construction of its coefficient data is still required to state the averaged theorem.

items.name: The averaged Colmez formula
items.statement: For E of degree 2g, sum over all 2^g CM types Phi: sum_Phi h_F(E,Phi) = sum_Phi sum_rho c_{rho,Phi}(L'(0,rho)/L(0,rho) + (1/2) log f_rho), using exactly the paper's conventions and the representations permitted there.
items.note: Existing paper jobs #1143 (AGHMP) and #1145 (Yuan-Zhang, including the 2023 erratum) own the deep proofs. Import those outputs; do not claim the individual Colmez conjecture. The published coefficient is one half, unlike an earlier arXiv formula.

items.name: Uniform character-combinatorics bounds in fixed dimension
items.statement: With g fixed, the possible normal-closure groups, relevant representation dimensions, and Colmez coefficient sizes form a bounded finite-combinatorial family; analytic constants arising from these data may therefore depend only on g.
items.note: Split off any trivial Artin factor as an explicit dimension-dependent constant before evaluating at s=1; its L-function has a pole at 1. The nontrivial-factor estimates must not be applied to it.

items.name: Polynomial conductor control sufficient for the height bound
items.statement: For the representations occurring in the fixed-degree Colmez expression, prove a bound log f_rho <= C_g(1+log |Disc(E)|), sufficient to absorb conductor terms into |Disc(E)|^epsilon.
items.note: This is the weaker sufficient contract, not an unchecked assertion of the source's literal f_rho <= |Disc(E)|. The precise conductor-discriminant comparison still needs a primary-source or pinned-library check.

items.name: Logarithmic derivatives at zero and one
items.statement: For the relevant nontrivial Artin representations with nonzero L(0,rho), the completed functional equation relates L'/L(0,rho) to L'/L(1,conjugate(rho)), a conductor logarithm, and archimedean terms bounded for fixed g. Track the conjugate representation and gamma factors.
items.note: No general Artin holomorphy conjecture is an allowed prerequisite. This input is scoped to the representations actually occurring in the height formula.

items.name: Subpolynomial estimates at one for the relevant Artin factors
items.statement: Establish the two-sided subpolynomial controls for the nonzero values at 1 of the relevant conjugate Artin representations, using Brauer induction and bounded-degree Hecke/Brauer-Siegel inputs; constants may be ineffective.
items.note: Do not infer a lower bound from an upper bound. Pole cancellation and trivial-character factors in a Brauer decomposition require explicit handling.

items.name: Subpolynomial derivative control needed by Corollary 3.3
items.statement: Establish |L'(1,conjugate(rho))| <= C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^epsilon for the factors in the averaged expression, or an equivalent direct logarithmic-derivative estimate sufficient for the height proof.
items.note: The source sketches Cauchy plus convexity. A Cauchy contour for an arbitrary Artin L-function cannot silently assume its conjectural entire continuation. The exact Hecke-level or averaged-formula implementation remains a verification gap.

items.name: Subpolynomial growth of primitive CM Faltings heights
items.statement: For every g and epsilon>0 there is C_{g,epsilon}>0 such that h_F(A) <= C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^epsilon for primitive maximal-CM A in S(E,Phi). The constant is uniform in E,Phi,A.

items.name: Rigidification by full three-torsion
items.statement: Starting from a polarized A with field of moduli F, adjoin the necessary third roots of unity and full level-3 data to rigidify the moduli problem and descend A to a number field whose degree over F is bounded solely in g.
items.note: This is a field-of-definition construction, not simply an assignment of coordinates to the coarse point.

items.name: Definition of endomorphisms after torsion rigidification
items.statement: Under the level-3 setup used in Lemma 4.1, apply Silverberg's homomorphism-definition result to define all endomorphisms and the necessary polarizations over the same extension; use the dual torsion and Weil pairing when passing to polarizations.
items.note: The exact hypotheses of Silverberg Proposition 2.3 still need a direct primary-source check.

items.name: Bounded extension of the field of moduli
items.statement: For a polarized dimension-g abelian variety A with field of moduli F, there exists F'/F of degree <=2*3^(4g^2) over which A, all its endomorphisms, and all its polarizations are defined.
items.note: This lemma is in the published version and absent from arXiv v5. It is indispensable in the proof below.

items.name: A common small field for the distant isogenous pair
items.statement: For A,B chosen using Proposition 2.2, descend the ideal quotient using endomorphisms defined over F_A'. The compositum F_A'F_B' defines both and has degree over F_A bounded by 4*3^(8g^2), as in the published proof.
items.note: Keep the polarized field-of-moduli choices compatible with the quotient; do not apply Theorem 2.3 over F_A without a model.

items.name: Discriminant lower bound for primitive maximal-CM moduli degrees
items.statement: For every g>=1 there are delta_g>0 and c_g>0 such that a polarized dimension-g A with primitive O_E-CM and End(A)=O_E satisfies [Q(A):Q] >= c_g |Disc(E)|^delta_g.
items.note: These are the same result, extracted once. The proof combines the distant-isogeny lower bound, subpolynomial height, quantitative isogeny estimate, and the field-of-definition bridge.

items.name: The centre order of a general CM point
items.statement: For a CM point x of A_g, define R_x as the centre of End(A_x), with its integral trace-form discriminant. This permits products, nonprimitive types, and nonmaximal orders; it is not replaced by the maximal order of one CM field.

items.name: Reflex field and reflex type
items.statement: For a primitive CM type (K,Phi), use the normal closure L and the stabilizer of the extended type to define the reflex field K* and reflex type Phi*. Keep embeddings and coset conventions explicit.

items.name: Reflex norm on ideals and principal elements
items.statement: Construct t_{K,Phi}:I_{K*}->I_K by the product of conjugate extended ideals prescribed by the reflex type; construct t' on elements and prove that principal ideals map to the corresponding principal ideals.

items.name: Class-group reciprocity map and its normal-closure version
items.statement: Descend the reflex norm to r:Cl(K*)->Cl(K) and define r_tilde=r composed with N_{L/K*}:Cl(L)->Cl(K). These domains must not be interchanged.

items.name: Bounded index for the class-group norm from the normal closure
items.statement: The image of N_{L/K*}:Cl(L)->Cl(K*) has index <=[L:K*], hence bounded in g; therefore a power lower bound for #im(r) passes, up to a dimension-dependent factor, to #im(r_tilde).

items.name: The polarized reciprocity subgroup H
items.statement: Inside Cl(K*), let H consist of ideal classes with r(I)=(a) and a*conjugate(a)=N_{K*/Q}(I), interpreted with the paper's fractional-ideal normalization. This is a subgroup of ker(r).
items.note: The printed norm subscript is incompatible with the domain of I; use the norm of the reflex-field ideal. Well-definedness under changing representatives must be proved.

items.name: The unit obstruction between the polarized and unpolarized kernels
items.statement: The discrepancy between ker(r) and H maps to O_{K0}^{times,+}/N_{K/K0}(O_K^times), via a*conjugate(a)/N_{K*/Q}(I), with kernel H. This quotient has order <=2^g, giving [ker(r):H]<=2^g.
items.note: Use totally positive units of the real field K0. Units of K0 squared are norms, and the real unit rank gives the bound.

items.name: CM reciprocity converts H into a moduli-degree bound
items.statement: Apply the CM main theorem with the reflex base field and polarized stabilizer made explicit, then compare absolute and relative degrees to obtain [Q(A):Q] <= C_g [Cl(K*):H] <= C_g*2^g*#im(r).
items.note: The exact equality in the source must not conflate the absolute field of moduli with a reflex-field compositum. The sufficient dimension-uniform inequality is the interface retained here; the base-field conventions remain to be checked directly.

items.name: Reduction from primitive reciprocity images to all CM orders
items.statement: For fixed g, the power discriminant lower bounds for the normal-closure reciprocity images attached to primitive CM types imply the Galois-orbit lower bounds for all CM points of A_g, including nonmaximal centre orders and nonsimple abelian varieties.
items.note: This is an imported nontrivial reduction, not a consequence of replacing an order by its maximal order. The detailed order/conductor/product dependencies in [20] remain to be extracted.

items.name: Galois-orbit bound for arbitrary CM points of A_g
items.statement: For each g there are b_g>0 and C_g>0 such that |Disc(R_x)| <= C_g * |Gal(Qbar/Q).x|^b_g for every CM point x in A_g(Qbar).

items.name: Siegel space, the arithmetic quotient, and a fundamental set
items.statement: For symmetric complex g-by-g matrices with positive definite imaginary part, form H_g and the quotient map pi:H_g->A_g(C) by Sp_(2g)(Z). Choose the semialgebraic Siegel fundamental-set setup used in the counting argument, including finite boundary multiplicities.
items.note: Do not assert that the coarse quotient is globally a free covering or that an open fundamental domain covers its boundary.

items.name: Special versus weakly special subvarieties
items.statement: Use Shimura data and the fixed-factor description to define special and weakly special subvarieties of A_g and their lifts. A weakly special subvariety may have a nonspecial fixed factor; the two notions are not identified.
items.note: Keep the Shimura-data owner as an import; LD.6 owns the stated functional-transcendence interface.

items.name: Reduction of the Andre-Oort argument to algebraic coefficients
items.statement: For an irreducible algebraic V over C, pass to irreducible components of the Zariski closure of its CM points, which is defined over Qbar, and then to a number field of definition. Proving the dense-CM form there gives the finite-maximal-special formulation.
items.note: This reduction needs its algebraic descent and Noetherian arguments, rather than an assumption that the original V was defined over Qbar.

items.name: Height and bounded degree for algebraic lifts
items.statement: Use the algebraic-point height convention of [15] and [16] for coordinates in a Siegel fundamental set, together with a fixed upper bound d_g on the relevant field degrees. Height must match the algebraic-point version of the counting theorem.
items.note: The extraction does not assert that the field generated by all coordinates always has degree exactly 2g; the verified downstream source only needs a degree bound depending on g.

items.name: Uniform bounded degree of CM lifts
items.statement: For fixed g, CM points admit algebraic lifts in the chosen fundamental set with degrees bounded by d_g independently of the discriminant.

items.name: Polynomial height bound for CM lifts
items.statement: For fixed g, suitable fundamental-set representatives y of a CM point x satisfy H(y) <= C_g |Disc(R_x)|^a_g for constants C_g,a_g depending only on g, with the degree and height conventions of the cited theorem.
items.note: The exact statement of [15] still needs a direct source check; keep the centre-order discriminant, not just the discriminant of a primitive CM field.

items.name: O-minimality of the real field with restricted analytic functions and exponentiation
items.statement: The structure R_an,exp is o-minimal, with its definable-set closure and cell-decomposition API.

items.name: Definability of the restricted Siegel uniformization
items.statement: The restricted uniformization on the chosen Siegel fundamental set is definable in R_an,exp, so pi^{-1}(V) intersect that set is definable for algebraic V.

items.name: The algebraic part of a definable set
items.statement: For T in a real affine space, T_alg is the union of its connected positive-dimensional semialgebraic subsets, with the convention needed by Pila-Wilkie. It is not the Zariski closure of T.

items.name: Pila-Wilkie with a fixed algebraic degree bound
items.statement: For definable T, a fixed degree bound d, and epsilon>0, the number of degree-<=d algebraic points of height <=X in T outside T_alg is O_{T,d,epsilon}(X^epsilon). Include the reduction from the rational-point theorem to bounded-degree algebraic points.

items.name: Many bounded-height lifts from a Galois orbit
items.statement: If V is defined over a number field F, the Gal(Qbar/F)-orbit of a CM point in V supplies at least its absolute orbit size divided by [F:Q] points in V. Invariance of the centre-order discriminant, the height bound, and finite lift multiplicities produce a power lower bound for the count in the definable preimage.

items.name: Bounded degree and bounded height give finitely many lifts
items.statement: For the fixed algebraic degree bound and any fixed height bound, only finitely many relevant algebraic coordinate tuples occur. Thus infinitely many distinct CM points force arbitrarily large counting parameters.
items.note: A likely existing height-theory import. Missing is provisional until exact pinned coverage is checked, not a proposal to duplicate Northcott.

items.name: Maximal semialgebraic pieces in a complex analytic set are algebraic
items.statement: A maximal connected irreducible semialgebraic subset of a complex analytic set, in the sense of [16], is a complex algebraic subset suitable for the Ax-Lindemann theorem.
items.note: One cannot apply Ax-Lindemann directly to an arbitrary real semialgebraic arc.

items.name: Hyperbolic Ax-Lindemann for A_g
items.statement: For algebraic V in A_g, every maximal irreducible complex algebraic subset of pi^{-1}(V) is weakly special in the precise lifted sense.
items.note: The conclusion is weakly special, not automatically special.

items.name: A weakly special subvariety through a CM point is special
items.statement: A weakly special subvariety of A_g containing a special (CM) point is special, by the fixed-factor Shimura description.

items.name: Only finitely many CM points avoid positive-dimensional special subvarieties
items.statement: For fixed V, combine the orbit/height lower bound with bounded-degree Pila-Wilkie and Ax-Lindemann to show that all but finitely many CM points of V lie on positive-dimensional special subvarieties contained in V.

items.name: Finite group types for maximal weakly special families
items.statement: For algebraic V in A_g, the group-theoretic and o-minimal argument of [16], Lemma 7.2, gives finitely many relevant semisimple Q-subgroups F (without compact factors) describing the positive-dimensional weakly special subvarieties by pi(F(R)^+ y).
items.note: The proof uses definability plus countability of rational group data, stabilizers, and normalizers. This is not merely cell decomposition; exact maximality conventions must be retained.

items.name: Induction on dimension through weakly special families
items.statement: Complete the finite-maximal-special argument using the finite family/group types, the fixed-factor Shimura descriptions, and induction on lower-dimensional parameter loci, as in [16], Theorem 7.1.
items.note: The final parameter-locus construction in [16] is a remaining direct-source check; the sketch in the 2018 paper alone is not a replacement.

items.name: Andre-Oort for A_g
items.statement: For every g>=1, every irreducible closed algebraic V in A_g contains only finitely many maximal special subvarieties. Equivalently, every irreducible subvariety with Zariski-dense CM points is special.
items.note: Scope is A_g in arbitrary dimension, not every Shimura variety. The two theorem numbers denote the same result.

items.name: Andre-Oort for the stated mixed-Shimura class
items.statement: The paper records the Andre-Oort consequence for every mixed Shimura variety whose pure part is a Shimura subvariety of A_g, via Gao's reduction and Theorem 4.2.
items.note: The precise scope is stated on printed p. 380: pure part a Shimura subvariety of A_g. This is not all mixed Shimura varieties. Gao's theorem and the interfaces realizing this consequence still require direct extraction.

routes.reason: LD.6 explicitly plans the Pila-Zannier/Andre-Oort branch with separate arithmetic, definability and functional-transcendence imports. This paper refines that existing branch; it does not justify a duplicate Andre-Oort roadmap. Foundational imports named in these items remain owned by their existing geometric and height-theory roadmaps.

The Hodge-line and stable-height machinery is already planned here. The Bost lower bound is a source-level sharpening needed by its height exports, not a second definition of Faltings height. Averaged CM heights and quantitative minimum-isogeny degrees are intentionally not subsumed by this route.
